metadata.research_goal: Create backend-ready volleyball knowledge for match IQ, scouting, team tactics, phase analysis, rotation-specific decision rules, performance indicators, and tactical learning progressions from beginner to advanced levels.

source_refs.title: Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028
source_refs.notes: Defines legal match structure, rotations, team hits, substitutions, time-outs, libero constraints, interruptions, and delay rules. Used for tactical decision boundaries, not for technique claims.

source_refs.title: Coaches Manual Level II
source_refs.notes: Covers serve receive formations, switching, attack balance, block-defense, scouting reports, match preparation, game plans, and rotation-based offensive combinations.

source_refs.title: Technical and Data Report VNL 2024
source_refs.notes: Modern elite benchmark source for attack efficiency, in-system and out-of-system efficiency, positive reception, serve aces and errors, blocks, team errors, crunch-time performance, and medal-profile KPIs.

source_refs.title: Opponent Analysis and Scouting Reports
source_refs.notes: Practical scouting checklist for offensive tendencies by rotation, serve receive formations, hitter shot charts, blocking schemes, defensive formations, and use of alternate receive patterns.

source_refs.title: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!
source_refs.notes: Used for block-defense reading rules: block as first line of defense, pass-set-hitter visual sequence, hitter shoulder and approach cues, line/angle calls, and tip coverage.

source_refs.title: Recipe for a Setter
source_refs.notes: Used for setter match IQ: directing receive changes, using hot hitters, exploiting blocker mismatches, changing offensive tempo, and knowing options in every rotation.

source_refs.title: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero
source_refs.notes: Used for libero tactical rules: absorbing large passing zones, baiting serving teams, free-ball priority, hitter coverage, and second-setter responsibilities in transition.

source_refs.title: Lesson Plans
source_refs.notes: Used for beginner and intermediate learning design: gamelike drills, random practice, whole skill practice, and scoring constraints rather than isolated blocked repetitions.

source_refs.title: Simplified Youth Rules
source_refs.notes: Used for beginner tactical progressions, youth service-run limits, positive versus negative errors, three-contact learning, simple rotation awareness, and safety around net play.

source_refs.title: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review
source_refs.notes: Reviews adult male volleyball match-analysis literature and supports using game actions, phase context, technical-tactical indicators, and outcome-linked skills rather than raw box score totals alone.

source_refs.title: Effect of Team Level on Skill Performance in Volleyball
source_refs.notes: Classic Olympic match-analysis study linking team level with skill performance in serve, reception, spike, block, and dig. Used for level-sensitive KPI weighting.

source_refs.title: Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory
source_refs.notes: Analyzed 2010 senior men's World Championship matches and reported serve points, reception errors, and blocking-related variables as important discriminators of match outcome.

source_refs.title: Game-Related Performance Factors in Four European Men's Professional Volleyball Championships
source_refs.notes: Uses professional league match data to evaluate outcome predictors and supports tracking service errors, service points, reception errors, blocked balls, attack points, number of scorers, and team level.

source_refs.title: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness
source_refs.notes: Top-level men's match sample linking front receiver attack effectiveness with reception-attack transition, setter position, and team rotation. Used for serving-target and rotation-pressure rules.

source_refs.title: A Comparative Analysis of Volleyball Skills in Balanced Sets for Men and Women in Asian Competitions
source_refs.organization_or_author: Drikos, Fatahi, Ahmed, Molavian, Giatsis, and Shakeri
source_refs.notes: Balanced-set analysis from 2023 AVC Challenge Cup; supports attack win percentage, serve win percentage, and attack-after-reception as important set outcome indicators while noting gender and context differences.

source_refs.title: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball
source_refs.notes: Journal of Human Sport and Exercise article on timeout use and psychological momentum in women's Division I volleyball. Used cautiously for timeout timing and reset logic.

source_refs.title: The Timeout in Sports: A Study of Its Effect on Volleyball
source_refs.notes: Frontiers in Psychology study on timeout effects in youth volleyball, using lost-rally and score-difference variables. Used as supporting evidence for context-dependent timeout logic.

source_refs.title: Training Without a Net or Friends
source_refs.notes: Applied player-development resource used for post-serve recovery and gamelike solo or small-group training concepts.

source_refs.title: Why Should I Run a 6-3 or 6-6?
source_refs.notes: Development-oriented resource on broad participation, smaller-sided learning, and delaying narrow specialization. Used for beginner match-IQ progression and system-learning context.

key_concepts.concept: Volleyball match IQ starts by separating the rally into phases instead of treating every contact as an isolated skill.
key_concepts.details: Useful phase labels are serve pressure, side-out after serve receive, transition or breakpoint after defending, and extended-rally counterattack. The same attack outcome means different things when it follows a perfect pass, a dig under stress, or a free ball.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

key_concepts.concept: Side-out is the receiving team's first-order stabilizer because it stops the opponent's serving run and restores service.
key_concepts.details: The side-out chain is reception quality, setter availability, attacker readiness, set tempo, attack choice, and coverage. Higher levels should track side-out by rotation and pass quality; beginner teams should first track whether they can receive, set a hittable ball, and send a controlled attack over the net.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness
A Comparative Analysis of Volleyball Skills in Balanced Sets for Men and Women in Asian Competitions

key_concepts.concept: Transition is the serving team's chance to convert serve pressure and defensive control into a point.
key_concepts.details: The transition sequence begins with block-defense organization, then dig quality, second-setter availability, counterattack tempo, attack choice, and hitter coverage. Transition effectiveness is a major separator at stronger levels because teams must score after defending good attacks, not only after receiving easy balls.
source_refs: Game-Related Performance Factors in Four European Men's Professional Volleyball Championships
So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

key_concepts.concept: Serving runs are created by repeatable pressure, not only aces.
key_concepts.details: A run can come from aces, predictable out-of-system balls, attacking receivers who cannot transition, setters forced off the net, or emotional pressure after repeated poor first contacts. The backend should store serving-run triggers, risk level, and stop rules separately from raw ace count.
source_refs: Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory

key_concepts.concept: Every rotation is a different tactical context because setter location, hitter count, receiver responsibilities, approach lanes, and block matchups change.
key_concepts.details: Rotation analysis should not only list who is on court. It should identify setter path, front-row attacker count, which hitter has receive-to-attack load, likely first tempo availability, opponent block matchups, serve target choices, and the planned fallback if pass quality drops.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

key_concepts.concept: Setter tendencies should be modeled conditionally, not as simple favorite-hitter labels.
key_concepts.details: A meaningful setter profile separates choices by pass quality, rotation, setter front-row or back-row status, score pressure, hitter availability, opponent blocker, and previous rally outcome. The goal is a probabilistic scout that predicts likely options while leaving room for deception.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

key_concepts.concept: Hitter scouting links set location and body cues to shot distribution.
key_concepts.details: Shot charts should split in-system and out-of-system attempts, line versus cross, sharp angle versus deep corner, tool attempts, tips, roll shots, error zones, and performance against different block looks. A hitter's tendency on a perfect set may be irrelevant when the set is tight, inside, or off the net.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

key_concepts.concept: A serving target plan is a tactical hypothesis that should connect a target to an expected constraint on the opponent's offense.
key_concepts.details: Valid reasons to target a zone include weak receiver, receiver-to-attacker transition cost, setter movement interference, seam confusion, short-ball vulnerability, forcing a non-preferred attacker, or reducing middle availability. If the target does not change the opponent's offense or produce errors, it should be revised.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness
How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

key_concepts.concept: Block and floor defense work as one contract: the block takes away a declared lane and defense loads the expected remaining spaces.
key_concepts.details: Block calls should be translated into backcourt starting positions and responsibilities for hard-driven ball, tip, roll, and tool coverage. When blockers change line/angle responsibility without communicating, defenders lose the read structure behind them.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

key_concepts.concept: Timeouts are best treated as reset and adjustment tools, not guaranteed momentum stoppers.
key_concepts.details: Research on volleyball timeouts is mixed, but useful patterns support calling timeouts earlier in opponent scoring runs and while the set is still close. A timeout script should contain one emotional reset cue, one tactical instruction, and one next-rally plan.
source_refs: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball
The Timeout in Sports: A Study of Its Effect on Volleyball
key_concepts.source_note: The timeout studies were used as supporting evidence from search results and abstracts; they should be rechecked before production ingestion if exact thresholds are encoded as hard rules.

key_concepts.concept: Substitution decisions are tactical resource choices constrained by rule set, rotation order, player readiness, and remaining substitutions.
key_concepts.details: Under FIVB rules, teams have limited substitutions per set. A substitution should have a clear tactical reason: improve a serve, pass a rotation, block a matchup, protect an injured or overloaded player, add a double substitution pattern, or change emotional rhythm. The cost is loss of flexibility later in the set.

key_concepts.concept: The most useful stats depend on competitive level and data quality.
key_concepts.details: Beginner teams benefit from serve-in rate, first-contact playable rate, three-contact attempts, and unforced errors. Intermediate teams can add pass rating, side-out percentage, breakpoint percentage, attack efficiency, and rotation scoring. Advanced teams should split all core stats by phase, rotation, pass quality, matchup, setter position, score state, and pressure moment.
source_refs: Effect of Team Level on Skill Performance in Volleyball
Game-Related Performance Factors in Four European Men's Professional Volleyball Championships

key_concepts.concept: A scout is only useful if players can act on it during rallies.
key_concepts.details: Advanced scouting reports can contain many variables, but the player-facing plan should be small: serve this zone for this reason, block this hitter this way, defend this lane, expect this set in this rotation, and use this fallback if the read is wrong.

key_concepts.concept: In-match adjustment should follow observe, compare, decide, communicate, test, and retain-or-revert.
key_concepts.details: A change should be triggered by repeated evidence such as two or more side-out failures in the same rotation, a hitter beating the same block-defense plan, a server scoring through the same seam, or the opponent changing its lineup or receive pattern. One-rally noise should not override a sound plan.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

technical_models.model: Rally phase model for tactical tagging

phases.ends_when: The receiving team's first attack is completed or the serve ends the rally.
phases.primary_goal: Create an ace, error, predictable pass, or limited opponent attack while controlling service-error risk.

phases.ends_when: Receiving team wins the point, loses the point, or the rally enters post-attack continuation.
phases.primary_goal: Turn serve receive into a controlled first attack and end the opponent's serving run.

phases.starts_when: Serving team defends the opponent's attack or receives a free/down ball.
phases.ends_when: Serving team counterattacks or loses the continuation.
phases.primary_goal: Convert block-defense quality into a point while retaining enough organization to cover the counterattack.

phases.starts_when: The rally continues beyond the first side-out and first transition attack.
phases.primary_goal: Maintain organization under scramble conditions, identify the first high-quality swing, and avoid giving away the point.

technical_models.coaching_use: Tag every rally by phase first, then by skill. This avoids confusing a transition setting problem with a generic attacking problem or a serving-target problem with a passing problem.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

decision_steps: Stabilize first contact to a setter-accessible target.
If pass is positive, keep middle and pipe threats live where level appropriate.
If pass is off the net, select high-percentage outlet with clear coverage.
If the receiver must also attack, evaluate whether the serve location delayed the approach.
After the rally, tag the failure point as pass, setter access, hitter readiness, shot choice, coverage, or opponent defense.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

decision_steps: Use the serve and block plan to make the dig more predictable.
If the setter digs first contact, route second contact to trained second setter.
On a perfect or free-ball transition, run the fastest safe option for the level.
On a poor dig, prioritize a high-ball swing or controlled attack that keeps coverage organized.
Score the transition phase separately from side-out so counterattack training needs are visible.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!
How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

analysis_rules: Map rotation labels to the team's own lineup convention before applying rules.
Separate back-row setter rotations from front-row setter rotations because attacker count and setter dump threat change.
Flag any rotation where a front-row receiver must pass and still hit a first-tempo or pin route.
Flag any rotation where the setter's path crosses a passing seam or is vulnerable to short serves.
Store actual side-out percentage and opponent breakpoint percentage for each rotation.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

technical_models.scouting_warning: Do not overfit a setter profile from a small sample. Use tendency bands and update with live match evidence.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

technical_models.coaching_use: Translate the profile into a simple block-defense plan: take away the highest-value shot, bait the low-efficiency shot, and assign tip coverage.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!
Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory
How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero
Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

technical_models.model: Bench decision logic for timeouts and substitutions
timeout_script: Name the next serve receive or serve target.
Assign one player to confirm the on-court call.
Avoid overloading players with a full scouting report.
source_refs: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball
The Timeout in Sports: A Study of Its Effect on Volleyball

technical_models.model: Performance indicator ladder by competitive level

beginner_stats.reason: Rally scoring makes missed serves immediately costly, and beginners often lose points before tactical play starts.
Measures whether the team can keep the rally alive and create a second contact.
Encourages serve receive, set, and attack structure instead of panic overpasses.
At entry level, reducing free points usually beats complex scouting.

intermediate_stats.reason: Captures whether the team can stop serving runs and convert receive into points.
Captures whether the serving team can score after serve pressure and defense.
Links receive quality to setter options and first attack quality.
More informative than kill count because it includes errors and blocks.
Identifies rotations that produce or leak runs.

advanced_stats.reason: Shows whether a rotation fails because of serve receive, setter path, or attack matchup.
Measures how well the team converts high-quality first contacts.
Measures adaptability when pass or dig quality breaks the planned offense.
Connects serving target to opponent reception, side-out, and error outcomes.
Captures transition scoring after dig, block touch, free ball, or down ball.
Tracks whether choices remain effective in high-leverage score states.

source_refs: Effect of Team Level on Skill Performance in Volleyball
Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory
A Comparative Analysis of Volleyball Skills in Balanced Sets for Men and Women in Asian Competitions

technical_models.model: Beginner to advanced tactical learning progression

levels.focus: Know court zones, rotation direction, three-contact structure, base positions, calling the ball, and serving in with purpose.
player_tasks: Call mine or help before first contact.
Know where the setter target is.
Recover to a simple base after sending the ball over.
Serve to a large zone instead of only trying to clear the net.
Understand that a high playable ball is usually a good miss.
avoid: Overloading players with full opponent scouting reports.
Running complex switches before players understand legal rotations.
Using double blocks when players cannot jump and land safely near the net.

levels.focus: Connect rotations, serve receive patterns, side-out, breakpoint, block-defense calls, and simple opponent tendencies.
player_tasks: Know the team's strongest and weakest side-out rotations.
Serve a named zone for a named reason.
Make line or angle block calls and defend behind them.
Recognize when the setter is front row or back row.
Use a planned fallback ball when pass quality is poor.
avoid: Changing tactics after one unlucky rally.
Tracking advanced stats without enough data quality.
Giving every player more than one or two scout cues at a time.

levels.focus: Use phase, rotation, matchup, pass-quality, score-state, and tendency data to adapt during the match.
player_tasks: Read setter choices by rotation and pass quality.
Adjust serve target when the opponent changes receive pattern.
Use block-defense contracts based on set location and hitter profile.
Separate side-out problems from transition problems in feedback.
Apply timeout and substitution decisions as resource-management choices.
avoid: Prioritizing raw kills over efficiency and phase context.
Ignoring fatigue and injury risk when tactical plans overload one player.

tactical_rules.rule: Protect setter access before chasing perfect pass location.
tactical_rules.rationale: A slightly off-target but setter-accessible pass keeps the team in offense; a low, tight, or overpassed ball often hands the opponent a direct scoring chance.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the serve creates conflict or late movement, prioritize a high playable ball to the setter zone or middle of court before attempting a perfect target.

tactical_rules.rule: Diagnose side-out failure by chain link, not by final attacker.
tactical_rules.rationale: The hitter may receive blame for a low-efficiency swing that was actually caused by poor pass quality, setter path, delayed transition, or predictable out-of-system setting.
tactical_rules.if_then: If side-out fails twice in one rotation, tag pass quality, setter location, hitter readiness, set choice, block matchup, and shot decision before changing personnel.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

tactical_rules.rule: Serve a front-row receiver when the serve location can reduce that player's attack readiness.
tactical_rules.rationale: Top-level research indicates that the reception-to-attack transition can reduce front receiver spike effectiveness in some rotations and setter-position contexts.
tactical_rules.if_then: If a front-row hitter must pass and then run a major first-ball route, serve a zone that adds movement away from the intended approach lane; abort if the libero or another passer absorbs the target cleanly.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

tactical_rules.rule: Do not serve the weakest passer automatically; serve the target that most limits the opponent's next attack.
tactical_rules.rationale: A weak passer matters most when the resulting pass removes middle tempo, forces a predictable pin, or creates an error. If a weak passer still produces high easy balls to the opponent's best attacker, another target may be better.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the weak passer's average pass still allows the opponent's preferred offense, test a seam, short target, or transition-load target instead.

tactical_rules.rule: Increase serve risk only when the expected pressure outweighs the immediate point cost.
tactical_rules.rationale: Elite data tracks aces and errors together because a high-ace plan can lose value if errors arrive in low-leverage or tactically unnecessary moments.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the team has just missed a serve, is leading late by one, or faces an opponent rotation already struggling to side out, choose a pressure-in serve before a maximum-risk serve.
source_refs: Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory

tactical_rules.rule: Keep a successful serving plan until the opponent proves an adjustment.
tactical_rules.rationale: Serving runs often come from repeated seam conflict or transition overload. Changing targets too early can release pressure.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the same target produces two poor passes, a direct error, or a predictable out-of-system ball, repeat the target or adjacent seam until the opponent changes shape or passer responsibility.

tactical_rules.rule: After calling timeout to receive, name the next pass responsibility and first-ball option.
tactical_rules.rationale: A timeout works best as a focused reset. Players need a simple next-rally plan, not a long review of all match problems.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the timeout was called during an opponent serving run, identify the target passer or seam owner, the setter fallback, and the preferred high-percentage first swing.
source_refs: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball
The Timeout in Sports: A Study of Its Effect on Volleyball

tactical_rules.rule: Consider timeout early in a damaging run rather than after the set has separated.
tactical_rules.rationale: Timeout research suggests better usefulness when score margins are still small and before momentum has fully built. This should be a guide, not an automatic rule.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent scores two or three consecutive points through the same pattern and the set is still within roughly three points, consider timeout if no on-court adjustment is ready.
source_refs: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball
The Timeout in Sports: A Study of Its Effect on Volleyball

tactical_rules.rule: Use a tactical substitution only when the expected gain in that rotation is worth the lost future flexibility.
tactical_rules.rationale: FIVB substitutions are limited, so a serving, passing, blocking, or attacking sub must be weighed against endgame needs and legal reentry constraints.
tactical_rules.if_then: If a serving specialist is likely to create real pass pressure and the team has enough substitutions left for planned reentries, use the sub; if the server only adds marginal pressure, preserve the resource.

tactical_rules.rule: Track each rotation as a mini-game with its own side-out rate, point scoring rate, serve target, and first-ball plan.
tactical_rules.rationale: Team averages hide whether a team loses one rotation badly and survives the others. Rotation-level tracking makes adjustments precise.
tactical_rules.if_then: If one rotation is minus three or worse across two cycles, adjust receive shape, first-ball route, serving target, or substitution plan before changing the entire system.

tactical_rules.rule: In back-row setter rotations, protect the setter path and preserve three front-row attack threats where the level supports it.
tactical_rules.rationale: Back-row setter rotations can offer three front-row attackers, but a difficult setter path or poor pass can remove tempo and make the offense predictable.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent serves the setter path or the receiver next to the setter, adjust passing lanes, release timing, or first-ball tempo before assuming the attackers are the problem.

tactical_rules.rule: In front-row setter rotations, account for reduced front-row hitter count while using setter attack, tempo, and matchup deception.
tactical_rules.rationale: The front-row setter can attack or dump and can manipulate blockers, but the team often has fewer pure front-row attacking options.
tactical_rules.if_then: If blockers ignore the setter, use second-contact threat or fast tempo; if blockers commit to the setter, release hitters into the space created.

tactical_rules.rule: Prepare a secondary receive pattern for rotations that opponents will target.
tactical_rules.rationale: Scouting resources emphasize whether teams use alternate serve receive formations when in trouble. Without a practiced secondary pattern, in-match adjustments often create overlap or seam confusion.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent scores twice into the same receive seam, switch to the practiced alternate pattern and name the new seam owner before the next serve.

tactical_rules.rule: Scout repeat behavior after kills, errors, and timeouts separately.
tactical_rules.rationale: Some setters feed a hot hitter, some move away from an error, and some run scripted plays after stoppages. Aggregated set distribution can hide these patterns.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the setter repeatedly returns to the same hitter after a kill in a specific rotation, shade the block-defense plan on that next comparable pass quality.

tactical_rules.rule: Separate setter choices on perfect passes from choices on poor passes.
tactical_rules.rationale: An advanced offense may be balanced in system but predictable out of system. Blocking plans should key the real available options.
tactical_rules.if_then: If pass quality pulls the setter beyond the attack line or sideline, release blockers and defenders toward the most likely high-ball outlet rather than honoring unavailable first-tempo options.

tactical_rules.rule: Read hitter choices through set location before applying generic shot charts.
tactical_rules.rationale: A hitter's line, cross, tip, and tool choices change when the set is tight, inside, outside the antenna, or off the net.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the set is tight, expect faster downward or tool attempts; if the set is off the net, load deeper angle and roll-shot coverage; if the set is outside the antenna, protect sharp cross and emergency recycle.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

tactical_rules.rule: Identify left-handed attackers during warm-up and adjust block hand and defensive expectations.
tactical_rules.rationale: Handedness changes natural contact angle, especially from right-side or out-of-system positions.
tactical_rules.if_then: If a hitter is left-handed, confirm blocking shoulder alignment and defender starting spots before that hitter's first front-row rotation.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

tactical_rules.rule: Every block plan needs a line or angle responsibility that backcourt defenders understand.
tactical_rules.rationale: A block that takes no declared space leaves defenders guessing and reduces dig quality.
tactical_rules.if_then: If blockers call line, backcourt loads angle and tip seams; if blockers call angle, line defender protects line and deep corner.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

tactical_rules.rule: Commit block only when the opponent's pass, setter tendency, and attacker threat justify leaving other options exposed.
tactical_rules.rationale: Commit blocking can stop elite middles or scripted plays, but it creates openings if used without enough information.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent's positive pass plus rotation tendency sends first tempo at high frequency, commit selectively; if pass quality drops, return to read or release blocking.

tactical_rules.rule: Treat free balls as planned scoring opportunities, not relief rallies.
tactical_rules.rationale: Free balls give the receiving team time to organize pass, setter, attack routes, and coverage. Poor free-ball conversion is a tactical failure.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent sends a free ball, assign the best ball-control player to first contact, run the planned free-ball offense, and measure conversion rate after the set.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

tactical_rules.rule: Train a second-setter plan for every defensive rotation.
tactical_rules.rationale: When the setter digs the first ball, transition quality depends on whether another player can set a hittable ball with tempo and location.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the setter takes first contact, the libero or assigned second setter should move immediately to the setting zone while hitters call available routes.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

tactical_rules.rule: Use hitter coverage to permit aggressive but intelligent attacks against strong blocks.
tactical_rules.rationale: A team that covers well can challenge the block without turning every blocked ball into an immediate point for the opponent.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent block is scoring through stuffs, improve coverage spacing and tool-recycle options before telling hitters only to avoid the block.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero
Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory

tactical_rules.rule: Beginner tactical learning should be limited to court zones, communication, serve target, base, and three-contact intent.
tactical_rules.rationale: Beginners need repeatable perception-action habits before complex scouting or switching systems.
tactical_rules.if_then: If players cannot consistently receive and send a playable second ball, delay rotation-specific opponent scouting and train gamelike first-contact decisions.

tactical_rules.rule: Intermediate teams should connect simple scouting to a small number of practiced choices.
tactical_rules.rationale: At this level, a useful game plan is usually one serve target, one block-defense call, one receive adjustment, and one transition fallback per major rotation problem.
tactical_rules.if_then: If a scouting point cannot be practiced before the match or explained in one sentence to the player responsible, do not make it a primary cue.

tactical_rules.rule: Advanced teams should combine pre-match scouting with live evidence and phase-specific data.
tactical_rules.rationale: At high levels, opponents adjust. The original scout must be revised when the setter, receiver, or coach changes the pattern.
tactical_rules.if_then: If live data contradicts the scout across a meaningful sample in the same rotation and pass-quality context, update the on-court call and record the reason.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

tactical_rules.rule: In high-leverage points, simplify the plan to the team's best trained option unless the opponent has clearly taken it away.
tactical_rules.rationale: Pressure reduces tolerance for ambiguous cues. Elite data tracks crunch-time efficiency because execution under score stress matters.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the score is late and close, choose the serve target, pass pattern, and first-ball route that players have executed most reliably in that match context.

tactical_rules.rule: Change one tactical variable at a time when possible.
tactical_rules.rationale: Multiple simultaneous changes make it difficult to know whether the adjustment worked and can create player confusion.
tactical_rules.if_then: If a rotation is failing, first adjust receive shape or first-ball choice; if that fails, then consider personnel or system changes.

tactical_rules.rule: Use libero range to counter serving plans that overload outside hitters, but do not create hidden seams.
tactical_rules.rationale: A libero can pass a larger area and free attackers, but only if adjacent passers know the new seam responsibilities.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent repeatedly serves an outside hitter to reduce attack readiness, expand libero responsibility or move the hitter out of receive; announce the new seam owner.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero
Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

tactical_rules.rule: When the opponent changes receive pattern, re-scout before repeating the old target.
tactical_rules.rationale: A target that worked against a three-passer pattern may fail against a two-passer, four-passer, or libero-expanded pattern.
tactical_rules.if_then: If the opponent changes passer count or moves the libero, identify the new seams, setter path, and receiver-to-attack load before the next serve plan is called.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

tactical_rules.rule: Do not use raw kill count alone to evaluate attackers or tactics.
tactical_rules.rationale: Attack efficiency, error rate, block rate, phase, pass quality, and set context are needed to know whether an attack plan is actually working.
tactical_rules.if_then: If one hitter has many kills but low efficiency or high blocked rate, adjust shot selection, set location, or matchup rather than automatically increasing volume.
source_refs: A Comparative Analysis of Volleyball Skills in Balanced Sets for Men and Women in Asian Competitions

physical_demands.demand: Repeated receive-to-attack and defend-to-attack transitions require acceleration, deceleration, approach re-timing, and jump readiness under short time constraints.
physical_demands.tactical_relevance: Serving plans that target front-row receivers are partly physical: they make attackers move, stabilize a platform, then rapidly rebuild approach rhythm.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

physical_demands.demand: Setter match IQ depends on repeated fast movement to the setting zone, body control from imperfect passes, jump-setting or dumping threat, and decision-making while moving.
physical_demands.tactical_relevance: Serving at setter path or forcing off-net passes raises both physical and cognitive load on the setter.

physical_demands.demand: Serving runs require repeated high-concentration serving and immediate sprint to defensive base after each serve.
physical_demands.tactical_relevance: A server who scores pressure but cannot recover to defensive position can leak transition points after the opponent handles the serve.
source_refs: Training Without a Net or Friends

physical_demands.demand: Block-defense tactics require repeated split-step readiness, lateral movement, jump timing, landing control, and fast floor defense reactions.
physical_demands.tactical_relevance: Committing to a block or loading a defensive zone changes physical starting positions and movement distances for multiple players.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

physical_demands.demand: Advanced scouting increases information load: players must perceive serve, pass, setter, hitter, block, score, and rotation cues under rally speed.
physical_demands.tactical_relevance: Too many cues can reduce execution quality. Match plans should be filtered into role-specific actionable cues.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Repeatedly assigning a front-row hitter large serve receive responsibility can reduce approach readiness and increase acute fatigue across passing, acceleration, and jumping tasks.
injury_or_load_risks.tactical_trigger: Opponent repeatedly serves the same attacking receiver or the team relies on that player for both primary passing and high attack volume.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use libero range, shift seams, remove the hitter from receive in targeted rotations, or change first-ball route to reduce immediate transition cost.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness
How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Aggressive blocking systems and crowded net play increase landing and net-contact risk, especially for youth or low-training-age athletes.
injury_or_load_risks.tactical_trigger: Double blocks, late close blocks, or commit blocks are introduced before players can jump, land, and avoid the net safely.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: At beginner levels, prioritize reading and floor defense until blockers can reach safely above the net and land under control; use one-player blocks when appropriate.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: High-risk jump serving can add shoulder, trunk, and landing load while increasing point-costly service errors under fatigue.
injury_or_load_risks.tactical_trigger: A player uses maximum-risk serves across long runs or late-set pressure without enough accuracy or recovery.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Use a serve error budget, mix pressure-in targets, and monitor service errors after long runs or extended matches.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Defensive adjustments that invite tips, sharp angles, or deep pursuit can increase diving, rolling, lunging, and collision exposure.
injury_or_load_risks.tactical_trigger: The block-defense plan leaves open spaces that require late emergency saves or multiple players pursue the same ball.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Clarify tip coverage, line/angle responsibilities, and communication calls; train emergency movements progressively rather than only in matches.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Poorly prepared substitutions can create delay sanctions, cold-entry errors, or confusion about rotation responsibilities.
injury_or_load_risks.tactical_trigger: A substitute enters without knowing serve target, defensive base, blocking assignment, or legal rotation position.
injury_or_load_risks.mitigation: Prepare substitution cards or verbal scripts, confirm role assignment before the player enters, and keep substitutes warm and tactically engaged.

training_implications.implication: Practice should include side-out, transition, free-ball, down-ball, and extended-rally scenarios rather than only isolated serve, pass, set, hit repetitions.
training_implications.application: Build drills that start with a serve or realistic first contact, then score the phase goal: side-out, breakpoint, counterattack, or free-ball conversion.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

training_implications.implication: Rotation-by-rotation learning should be practiced as small games with clear scoring constraints.
training_implications.application: Start each game in a specific rotation, give the opponent a planned serve target, and track whether the team executes its receive shape, first-ball option, fallback, and coverage.

training_implications.implication: A scouting report should become practice constraints before it becomes a match plan.
training_implications.application: If the opponent's setter favors a right-side attacker on positive passes, practice the serve target that reduces that pass quality, the block call if the set still goes there, and the defensive responsibility behind it.

training_implications.implication: Stats should be taught as cues for decisions, not as punishment labels.
training_implications.application: Pair each tracked stat with an action: low side-out prompts receive or first-ball changes; high serve errors prompt risk adjustment; poor counterattack prompts second-setter and hitter transition work.
source_refs: Effect of Team Level on Skill Performance in Volleyball

training_implications.implication: Beginner tactical curriculum should prioritize playability, spacing, and communication over opponent-specific scouting.
training_implications.application: Use small-sided or simplified games where players learn court zones, serve target, three contacts, setter target, base position, and safe net behavior.
source_refs: Why Should I Run a 6-3 or 6-6?

training_implications.implication: Intermediate players should learn how serve, receive, block, and defense connect tactically.
training_implications.application: Use one-scout-cue games: serve zone 5 to make the outside hit late, block angle and defend line, or move libero to absorb a seam. Debrief with side-out and breakpoint outcomes.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

training_implications.implication: Advanced training should integrate video, tagged data, and live adjustment rehearsal.
training_implications.application: Before competition, build rotation cards and setter/hitter tendency sheets. During practice, force the scout team to change receive patterns or set choices so players rehearse updating the plan.
source_refs: Match Analysis in Volleyball: A Systematic Review

training_implications.implication: Timeouts should be rehearsed as communication events.
training_implications.application: Practice thirty-second timeout scripts in scrimmages: one reset cue, one tactical correction, next rally responsibility, and confirmation from the on-court leader.
source_refs: Timeouts and Psychological Momentum in Volleyball

training_implications.implication: Every team needs a second-setter plan for transition when the setter defends first contact.
training_implications.application: Train libero and selected back-row players to set hittable balls from common dig zones, then require hitters to call available transition routes.
source_refs: How You Can Make a Huge Impact as a Libero

training_implications.implication: Players should practice when to keep, modify, or abandon a tactical plan.
training_implications.application: Use scrimmage constraints where the same serve target works twice, then the opponent changes receive. Players must identify the new target or return to pressure-in serving.

backend_records_to_create.name: Back-row setter rotation priority
backend_records_to_create.condition: Setter is in the back row and the system can use three front-row attackers.
backend_records_to_create.rule: Protect the setter path, preserve middle availability, and use three front-row options when pass quality allows.

backend_records_to_create.name: Front-row setter rotation priority
backend_records_to_create.condition: Setter is in the front row.
backend_records_to_create.rule: Account for fewer front-row hitters while using setter attack threat, tempo changes, and blocker manipulation.

backend_records_to_create.name: Setter conditional set distribution
backend_records_to_create.player_facing_translation: Expect this hitter in this rotation on this pass quality; block and defend this lane first.

backend_records_to_create.name: Hitter shot chart by context
backend_records_to_create.player_facing_translation: Block the highest-value lane and place defenders where the remaining shots are most likely.

backend_records_to_create.name: Attack efficiency
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Intermediate teams can track total attack efficiency; advanced teams should split by phase and pass quality.

backend_records_to_create.name: Side-out percentage
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Core team stat from intermediate upward; simplified for beginners as receive-to-playable-attack rate.
source_refs: Reception-Attack Transition in Volleyball: Analysis of Spike Effectiveness

backend_records_to_create.name: Breakpoint percentage
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Intermediate and advanced stat for evaluating serving runs and transition scoring.

backend_records_to_create.name: Serve receive pass rating
backend_records_to_create.formula: average ordinal rating of serve reception quality using the team's chosen scale
backend_records_to_create.recommended_scale: 0 to 3 or 0 to 4, with separate tags for ace/error, no attack, limited attack, and full offense
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Intermediate teams can rate pass quality; advanced teams should connect pass quality to side-out and first attack efficiency.

backend_records_to_create.name: Serve pressure profile
backend_records_to_create.formula: composite of ace rate, opponent poor-pass rate, opponent side-out allowed, and serve error rate
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Beginner teams track serve in and target zone; advanced teams track target expected value.
source_refs: Game-Related Volleyball Skills that Influence Victory

backend_records_to_create.name: Counterattack efficiency
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Advanced priority KPI; intermediate teams can begin with free-ball conversion and transition kill rate.
source_refs: Game-Related Performance Factors in Four European Men's Professional Volleyball Championships

backend_records_to_create.name: Rotation plus-minus
backend_records_to_create.level_use: Useful from intermediate upward for identifying rotations that need receive, serve, block, or substitution changes.

assessment_examples: Can rotate correctly after winning serve.
Can call seam responsibility before serve.
Can serve into a named half or zone at safe speed.
Can explain why a target zone was chosen.
Can identify front-row versus back-row setter.
Can execute a secondary receive pattern.
Can defend behind a line or angle block call.
source_refs: So You Want to be a Great Defender?! Learn to Read the Hitter!!

assessment_examples: Can update a serve plan after opponent receive adjustment.
Can distinguish a side-out problem from transition problem using tagged data.
Can call a block-defense plan based on pass quality and setter tendency.
Can recommend timeout or substitution with a rule-based rationale.
